status_note: Builder-authored and builder-tested against an independent in-test reference serializer and one non-Python (Node.js) implementation. NOT independently qualified; no Runtime or Control Plane implementation has been run against it. Contract preparation only: no source change. Incorporates Architect rulings OQ-1 to OQ-5 and Batch-4 rulings N-1, N-3, N-4, N-5, N-6 (2026-10-25). Revised after the PR #30 AI technical reviews, two rounds (parse order, input boundary, code point sort order, contract_version keying, projection-stage refusals, mapping vocabulary).

record_version.source: registry_successor/record.py (1 <= record_version <= common.MAX_INT); docs/s03-contract.md (record_version 1 to 2147483647, strictly increasing per record_id)
record_version.rationale: the record succession counter is already validated at this domain by the Registry and by the s03 record contract; the binding must accept exactly what a verified record pin can carry

selection_epoch.source: registry_successor/selection.py _epoch_ok (1 <= epoch <= common.MAX_INT); contract 7.1 (activation needs epoch strictly greater than the high-water)
selection_epoch.rationale: the selection epoch is a monotone counter with its own validator; its entry is independent of record_version and of every age; at the maximum no strictly higher epoch exists, so that scope cannot advance (fail closed, see spec 5.2)

trust_snapshot_version.source: registry_successor/verify.py:82 (strict int >= 1, no ceiling); registry_successor/common.py:102 (canonical_bytes writes unbounded Python ints); registry_conformance/highwater.py:187,442 (durable high-water and guard validation are floors only); registry_consumer/consumer.py:45 (MAX_VERSION applies to the record version only)
trust_snapshot_version.rationale: no source states a ceiling for the snapshot version, so the Architect ruling N-1 gives no source-justified bound and none is borrowed from record_version, selection_epoch or the age domain (2147483647). The strict bound the representation supports is the canonical-JSON safe integer range: the claim-carried binding is canonical JSON consumed by non-Python implementations, and 9007199254740991 (2**53 - 1) is the largest integer exact in every JSON implementation (RFC 8259 section 6, RFC 7493). Component-owner-derived: it narrows nothing the verifier accepts below it and refuses only values no interoperable implementation can carry exactly. A snapshot version above 2147483647 is valid here because the Registry verifier accepts it.

source_evidence.shows: the verifier accepts any strict int >= 1 for TrustSnapshot.version; no MAX_INT or other ceiling is applied (MAX_INT is applied only to record_version and selection epoch)
the 2**31-1 constant is used by record.py:40 and selection.py:62 for record_version and epoch only; no snapshot code references it
canonical_bytes writes a Python int as arbitrary-precision base-10 digits: the Registry serializer itself has no integer ceiling
the durable snapshot high-water (floors.snapshot_version) is validated as a strict int with a floor only; no ceiling; the claim-carried binding requires >= 1 (line 442)
the guard's binding validation of the snapshot version is a floor only
the consumer's only integer ceiling is for the record version (line 193); it stores and compares no snapshot version

status_max_age_seconds.source: Architect ruling OQ-1; ADR D-27 (AGE_MIN = 1 adopted)
status_max_age_seconds.rationale: technical representation ceiling only, not an operational setting; subject to the timestamp-safety qualification (observed_at + age must be representable, else refuse)

approval_max_age_seconds.rationale: same as status_max_age_seconds; a separate entry, not an alias

class_status_max_age_seconds.rationale: applies to every per-class value of the map; a separate entry, not an alias

policy_generation.source: ADR D-16 and contract 7.5 (approval generation, owner EXT-S3-4); contract 7.3 (ratchet generation)
policy_generation.rationale: reserved range note only: not a binding member, no vectors, no definition of the Control Plane generation here; a future generation counter is a monotone, never-reused counter and owns its own validated domain, so it is not tied to the 2^31-1 epoch or age domains; the bound is the largest integer exact in every JSON implementation (2^53 - 1) and is an open item for EXT-S3-4

decision.binding_creation: refused for every participation (field_invalid, stage projection)
decision.required: REFUSE (invalidity established; decision kind required_policy_unavailable); UNKNOWN_FAIL_CLOSED (HOLD) only if the consumer's authoritative state is indeterminate; never the caller policy
decision.optional: the projection refusal is never itself an authorization or a fallback; the consumer may fall back only through its authenticated, authorized optional-state determination (contract 4.3 and 7.4, EXT-S4-2) when the durable activation state permits it, and the fallback is recorded as an explicit absence or withdrawal evidence record carrying the original projection refusal code
decision.never: an unprojectable scope never yields overlay_not_applied or any ACCEPT by itself

Trust snapshot arrays are normalized by the serializer in code point order (never refused for order); a duplicate refuses trust_snapshot_invalid.

defect_mapping.note: stage is `projection`; the verified inputs stay verified; no binding is created for any participation. Required: REFUSE (UNKNOWN_FAIL_CLOSED only if consumer state is indeterminate), never the caller policy. Optional: no fallback by itself; any fallback is the consumer authenticated optional-state determination (contract 4.3, 7.4; EXT-S4-2) permitted by the durable activation state, recorded as an absence or withdrawal evidence record carrying projection_refusal_code=field_invalid. ruled_additive_codes.note: Architect ruling N-4: the three semantic distinctions are REQUIRED and enter the versioned v2 reason registry through an explicit additive amendment, written separately as a docs-only amendment PR. Until that amendment merges and a re-pinned outcome map exists, this work emits none of them as registry_code, keeps them disjoint from the 48 CODES_V2 entries, leaves the closed v1 vocabulary unchanged, and overloads no existing code. Names are the kit-local names of docs/conformance/README.md.

an encoded lone surrogate (CESU-8 style U+D800): not strict UTF-8: input_not_text (a str-only implementation applies the same strict decode before its API and refuses with the same code)
a UTF-8 byte order mark before a well formed document is not stripped: json_malformed
a \ud800 JSON escape is well formed text (no encoding error): the decoded value is not an identifier, so field_invalid at selection_id
9000 unclosed '[': syntax first (json_malformed), never json_nesting_too_deep, whatever a parser's recursion limit
a balanced array nested 10000 deep (20 KB, under the size limit): well formed, no number literal, no duplicate: json_nesting_too_deep
10000 levels with a float literal inside: number literals precede nesting, so json_number_unsupported at any depth
10000 levels balanced, then trailing text: syntax first, json_malformed
a duplicate key inside an object 10000 arrays deep: duplicates precede nesting, so json_duplicate_key at any depth
32768 '[' and 32768 ']' (exactly 65536 bytes): at the size limit, so the nesting refusal, not input_too_large
32769 pairs (65538 bytes): the size limit precedes everything

projection_stage_refusals.description: a verified trust snapshot with version 2^53 (the verifier accepts any strict int >= 1): the binding cannot carry it; field_invalid at the projection stage, member trust_snapshot_version
a snapshot version far above 2^53 (a 40-digit integer): the same refusal

projection_stage_refusals_rule: Any refusal at the projection stage (a scope token, a snapshot version, or any later verified-input-to-binding refusal) creates no binding for any participation and has exactly the participation effects of scope_projection_effects: required refuses (HOLD only if state is indeterminate), optional never falls back by the refusal itself, only through the authenticated optional-state determination; never overlay_not_applied or ACCEPT by itself. The effect function takes no member argument by construction.

projection_effect_invalid.description: participation must be exactly `required` or `optional` (case-sensitive); any other value is refused, never read as optional
a missing participation is refused, never read as optional

projection_effect_matrix_rule: Every projection-stage refusal kind (scope token, snapshot version, and each refused derivation of effective_policy_digest) has one and the same effect for a given participation, activation state and optional-state determination; the effect function takes no refusal kind and no member. Residuals recorded for the Architect, not decided here: (1) a refused projection leaves the scope reading never-activated, the state that permits the optional fallback; (2) a verified snapshot version above 2^53 - 1 affects every scope at once.
